experiment: recombinate of 24 compounds (OAV>1; 5 with OAV>100 + 19 with OAV>1) added to reconstructed matrix (deodorized cocoa powder + deodorized cocoa butter, 20% fat) at natural concentrations vs. real cocoa powder
result: overall sensory evaluation: recombinate "clearly indicated that the 24 compounds represented the typical sweet, cocoa-like odor of the real sample"; no similarity score or panel size in abstract
source_locator: abstract (Europe PMC / TUM portal record); full text not accessed
verbatim_note: "To establish their contribution to the overall aroma of the cocoa powder, these 24 compounds were added to a reconstructed cocoa matrix in exactly the same concentrations as they occurred in the cocoa powder."

matrix: two commercial dark chocolates (90% and 99% cocoa content)
experiment: reconstitution models in odorless sunflower oil containing all odorants with OAV>=1 at natural concentrations vs. original chocolates (28 odorants OAV>=1 in 90% CC; 30 in 99% CC)
result: "very high similarities" of reconstitution models to the chocolates; no numeric score in abstract
source_locator: abstract (Europe PMC); full text not accessed
verbatim_note: "very high similarities of the reconstitution models, containing all odorants with OAVs >= 1 in their naturally occurring concentrations in odorless sunflower oil as matrix, proved the correct identification and quantitation of all key odorants in both dark chocolates."

experiment: addition experiments: some chemicals added to the original dark or milk chocolate to validate their roles in the aroma property
compounds_omitted: compounds added not named in abstract
result: abstract states the relationship between aroma-active compounds and sensory perception "was verified"; no counts
